# Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Source of all malicious traffic below |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | Bound to 172.17.0.99 in DHCP Request/ACK (frames offering hostname `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT`) and confirmed in ARP replies (`18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4` ↔ `172.17.0.99`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP option 12 (Host Name) from 172.17.0.99; NBNS registrations `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`/`<20>`; DNS queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (domain BEPOSITIVE) | Kerberos `CNameString = afletcher`, realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM`, in AS-REQ/TGS traffic from 172.17.0.99 to the domain controller 172.17.0.17 |

LAN context: 172.17.0.0/24. Gateway 172.17.0.1 (MAC `00:02:4b:51:8c:b6`), domain controller/DNS 172.17.0.17, hostname `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19`, domain `bepositive.com` — all benign internal infrastructure.

## Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**. The provided Suricata alert export contains `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (Event #3.1504, 48 hits) fired directly on 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80 traffic. Behavior corroborates the signature: repeated `POST /foots.php` beacons carrying a pipe-delimited payload of the form `<code>|<bot-GUID>|<token>|<encrypted-blob>` (bot GUID observed: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`), a fixed legacy-IE user agent, and `nginx` empty-body 200 responses — a known Koi Stealer C2 checkin pattern. The Suricata alert set also independently flagged this same flow as `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (POST to a bare IP with a spoofed browser UA), consistent with the family's C2 style.

## Timeline / Delivery Chain

- **21:35:04–21:35:09 UTC+4 (17:35 UTC):** 172.17.0.99 opens a large TLS session (342/180 frames, ~479 KB) to **46.254.34.201:443**, SNI **`www.bellantonicioccolato.it`**. This is the only unusual, high-volume external connection immediately preceding the infection and is the likely delivery vector (compromised legitimate site serving the payload over HTTPS). Contents are TLS-encrypted, so no file name or hash could be extracted from this session — flagged as behavioral evidence, not confirmed.
- **21:35:06–21:35:12 UTC+4:** Within 2 seconds of that session, 172.17.0.99 begins contacting **79.124.78.197:80** directly by IP (no DNS lookup for it ever occurs — confirmed bare-IP C2, matching the "Dotted Quad" alert):
  - 3x `POST /foots.php` (Koi Stealer checkin, bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`)
  - `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` → server responds `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` (affiliate/loader-style ID handshake)
  - `POST /index.php` with an encrypted 105-byte binary body
- **21:35:07 UTC+4 → 22:31 UTC+4 (end of capture):** Sustained `POST /foots.php` beaconing to 79.124.78.197 at roughly 60–90 second intervals (48 total POSTs matched by the ETPRO signature), continuing for the full duration of the capture.

No executable, script, or other malware binary was transferred in the clear anywhere in this capture (`--export-objects http` yields no exe/dll/script; all foots.php exchanges are empty-body 200 responses; the payload session to 46.254.34.201 is TLS-encrypted). No file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this evidence.

## Indicators of Compromise
